_: PINNED IDENTITY OF THE FOUR EXTERNAL CHECKOUTS THE F3 CORPUS CENSUS READS (row R3-16).
The census produces the board's headline claims about real contracts. Before this manifest it read four
unpinned working directories, so re-running it later against drifted upstream sources would silently change
the denominator of every percentage the board quotes, and nothing would distinguish 'the compiler changed'
from 'the corpus changed'.
The sources are NOT vendored: this records identity, not content. It follows the pattern already set by
examples/solidity-by-example/SBE_SOURCE.md, which the census had simply not adopted.
WHY BOTH A COMMIT AND DERIVED COUNTS ARE RECORDED. An upstream commit alone does not pin the denominator,
because the denominator also depends on the harness's own exclusion sets. The solidity-by-example pin has
never been bumped, yet its in-scope count moved from 139 to 141 when exclusions were REMOVED from the
harness. fileCount and inScopeCount therefore pin the census's actual denominators, and fileSetDigest
catches a dirty working tree that leaves the commit looking correct.
Verify with layer3-corpus-pins.ts (verifyCorpusPins / assertCorpusPinsOrRefuse). A checkout that cannot be
verified is a NAMED REFUSAL, never a silent partial census.
A SECOND UNPINNED REPRODUCIBILITY PARAMETER, found while pinning the checkouts and recorded here because
it moves the same denominators. The recorded census reports 'files' per corpus but not the SAMPLING that
produced them, so a re-take at a different stride changes every solc-corpus percentage with nothing to
distinguish it from a compiler or corpus change.
mistswap 16, eacc 22 and solidity-by-example 141 are full in-scope populations (stride 1).
solc-corpus is NOT: the census records 407 files against an in-scope population of 4,876.
X125 ESTABLISHED THE STRIDE INSTEAD OF INFERRING IT. It was recorded here as INFERRED from ceil(4876/12)
= 407 plus the probe's 'at stride 12: 29 minutes' note. Neither is proof: the first shows 12 is CONSISTENT
with the counts, not that it is the only value that is, and the second is prose. The stride is now derived,
and the derivation is a uniqueness argument over the probe's own sampling rule, re-run by
CorpusPinsR316.test.ts rather than asserted here:
1. layer3-corpus-probe-f3.mjs:487 keeps a file when (inScope - 1) % stride == 0, so for a whole run
sampled == ceil(population / stride).
2. Searching every stride in 1..4876, exactly ONE satisfies ceil(4876 / s) == 407, and it is 12. The
neighbours miss: ceil(4876/11) = 444 and ceil(4876/13) = 376. Same search returns exactly [1] for the
other three corpora, which is the control that the method distinguishes strides at all.
3. A run truncated by F3_LIMIT would instead give sampled == (population - 1) / stride + 1 with
(population - 1) divisible by stride. 4875 = 3 * 5^3 * 13 and no divisor of it yields 407, so no
truncated run reproduces these counts either.
4. Independently of (3), layer3-corpus-probe-f3.mjs:609-613 REFUSES to overwrite the committed census
when F3_LIMIT, F3_CORPORA or F3_MERGE is set, so the recorded counts cannot be a truncation or a
merge of two runs at different strides.
So the solc-corpus row is a 1-in-12 systematic sample, 407 of 4,876. What is still NOT true is that the
probe RECORDS the stride: strideRecordedByProbe is false for every corpus, and that is the residual gap.
The above derives the stride from outputs; only the probe emitting F3_STRIDE into the census module would
read it from the source. Until then a stride that produced counts consistent with another stride would be
misread - the derivation is sound but it is arithmetic over results, not a record of the input.
Consequence for any consumer: a solc-corpus percentage has a denominator of 407 sampled files, not the
4,876 population, and must not be quoted as if the whole corpus were censused.

corpora.name: mistswap
notes: NOT REPRODUCIBLE FROM UPSTREAM, and this is the finding rather than a defect in the pin. The checkout
sits on a local unpushed commit ('old wip', 2026-07-19) that no remote branch contains, so a third
party cannot recreate this corpus from a public commit.
Measured scope of the divergence: 15 of the 16 census targets are byte-identical to the nearest public
ancestor 1f8622bb. Exactly one differs, contracts/bentobox/BentoBoxV1.sol (10 lines), and it is one of
the two load-bearing corpus anchors in layer3-target-corpus.md section 2.
The divergence is cosmetic rebranding (a domain-separator string 'BentoBox V1' -> 'Mirror V1', two
approval strings, a trailing space in a revert reason, STRATEGY_DELAY 2 weeks -> 2 minutes). It does
not touch the deposit path the corpus cites, so it is immaterial to what the census measures, but the
corpus is still not publicly recreatable and must not be described as if it were.
The working tree also carries unrelated dirt (package.json, patches/) outside contracts/.

starting with '@', which excludes the vendored @openzeppelin tree.

corpora.name: solidity-by-example
notes: Already pinned independently by examples/solidity-by-example/SBE_SOURCE.md, and the live checkout
matches that pin. This manifest records the same commit so the census does not depend on a pin
documented for a different harness.
inScopeCount is 141: 152 files less 10 EXCLUDED and 1 NEGATIVE. The board's SBE bench line quotes a
denominator of 139, which is older than the current exclusion set rather than evidence of drift; the
pin has never been bumped and the tree is clean at it.
The env var points at the checkout ROOT; the census reads contracts/src beneath it.

corpora.name: solc-corpus
notes: The whole checkout is the corpus (every .sol anywhere in it), so censusSubdir is the repository root.
fileCount 7343 and inScopeCount 4876 both match the denominators examples/solidity-corpus quotes,
which is independent corroboration that this checkout has not drifted since that scorecard was taken.
in-scope excludes the NEGATIVE and MULTIFILE buckets the probe classifies by file content.
